lessons.title: 1.1 Basic Routine Greetings
lessons.notes_html:
Meeting a New Friend

  • Amjad says: Good morning, Abbas. How are you?
  • Abbas replies: Good morning, Amjad. I am fine. Thank you.
  • Zaib is a new boy in class two. Abbas tells Amjad about him.
  • Amjad welcomes Zaib warmly: Hello Zaib. Welcome to class two.
  • Zaib says: Hello Abbas. Nice to meet you.
  • At the end Abbas says: Thank you. We are friends now.

Practice Note

This is a speaking-practice dialogue. Practise it in groups with your friends, taking the roles of Amjad, Abbas and Zaib.

Key Points

  • We say 'Good morning' when we meet someone in the morning.
  • We welcome a new friend with kind and happy words.

mcqs.q: What does Amjad say to Abbas in the morning?
options: Good morning, Abbas. How are you?
mcqs.why: Amjad greets Abbas in the morning with the words 'Good morning, Abbas. How are you?'

mcqs.q: How does Abbas reply to Amjad?
mcqs.why: Abbas replies that he is fine and thanks Amjad, because he is happy and well.

mcqs.q: Who is the new boy in class two?
mcqs.why: Zaib is the new boy in class two, and Abbas tells Amjad about him.

mcqs.q: Who tells Amjad about Zaib?
mcqs.why: Abbas tells Amjad about Zaib and introduces the new boy to him.

mcqs.q: How does Amjad welcome Zaib?
options: Hello Zaib. Welcome to class two.
mcqs.why: Amjad welcomes Zaib warmly and says, 'Hello Zaib. Welcome to class two.'

mcqs.q: What does Zaib say to Abbas?
mcqs.why: Zaib says, 'Hello Abbas. Nice to meet you,' when Abbas introduces him.

mcqs.q: What does Abbas say at the end of the dialogue?
mcqs.why: At the end Abbas says, 'Thank you. We are friends now,' so the three boys become friends.

mcqs.q: When do we say 'Good morning'?
mcqs.why: We say 'Good morning' when we meet someone in the morning time of the day.

mcqs.q: Abbas is happy and ____.
mcqs.why: The lesson tells us that Abbas is happy and well when he replies to Amjad.

mcqs.q: In which class is Zaib new?
mcqs.why: Zaib is new in class two, and Amjad welcomes him to class two.

lessons.title: 1.2 Introducing Myself and Others
lessons.notes_html:
About Kashaf

  • My name is Kashaf. Kashaf reads in class two.
  • Kashaf is six years old.
  • Kashaf likes drawing pictures.

About Bushra

  • Bushra is Kashaf's best friend.
  • Bushra likes reading stories.
  • Kashaf and Bushra sit together in the class.
  • They share their lunch and books with each other.
  • Bushra plays games with Kashaf in the park during recess.

Sight Words

Sight words are the words that are commonly used in the text: I, we, is, to, she, my, and, he, in, the, have, one, our, are, also.

Key Points

  • We tell our name, class and age when we introduce ourselves.
  • Good friends sit together, play together and share their things.

mcqs.q: What is the name of the girl who introduces herself in the lesson?
mcqs.why: The girl says, 'My name is Kashaf,' when she introduces herself in the lesson.

mcqs.q: In which class does Kashaf read?
mcqs.why: Kashaf reads in class two with her friends, as she tells us in the lesson.

mcqs.q: How old is Kashaf?
mcqs.why: Kashaf is six years old, as matched in the lesson: 'Kashaf is six years old.'

mcqs.q: Who is Kashaf's best friend?
mcqs.why: Bushra is Kashaf's best friend; she is kind and helpful to Kashaf.

mcqs.q: What does Kashaf like doing?
mcqs.why: Kashaf likes drawing pictures; she draws neat and beautiful pictures.

mcqs.q: What does Bushra like doing?
mcqs.why: Bushra likes reading stories and reads stories in her free time.

mcqs.q: What do Kashaf and Bushra share with each other?
mcqs.why: Kashaf and Bushra share their lunch and books with each other every day.

mcqs.q: Where do Kashaf and Bushra sit?
mcqs.why: Kashaf and Bushra sit together in the class and also play together in the park.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a sight word from the lesson?
mcqs.why: Sight words are commonly used words like I, we, is and the, which appear again and again in the text.

mcqs.q: Which word comes first in alphabetical order?
mcqs.why: In alphabetical order apple comes first, then book, then queen, and zebra comes last.

lessons.title: 1.3.1 Consonant Digraphs
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Digraph?

  • A consonant digraph is a combination of two consonant letters making one sound.
  • Examples of digraphs: sh, ch, th, ph, ng.

Words with Digraphs

  • ph at the beginning: phone, photo. ph at the ending: graph, digraph.
  • th at the beginning: thumb, thick. th at the ending: mouth, teeth.
  • ng at the ending: king, ring. No English word begins with 'ng'.

Complete the Words

  • chin, path, sing, three, shining, photo, cloth, dolphin, graph.

Key Points

  • Two consonant letters together can make only one sound.
  • The digraph 'ng' never comes at the beginning of an English word.

mcqs.q: A consonant digraph is two consonant letters making ____ sound.
mcqs.why: A consonant digraph is the combination of two consonant letters making one sound, like sh, ch, th, ph and ng.

mcqs.q: Which pair of letters is a consonant digraph?
mcqs.why: The letters ph make one sound together, so ph is a consonant digraph; the others are vowel pairs.

mcqs.q: Which word has 'ph' at the beginning?
mcqs.why: Phone begins with the digraph ph; graph has ph at the end, and mouth and king have other digraphs.

mcqs.q: Which word has 'ph' at the ending?
mcqs.why: Graph ends with the digraph ph, while photo and phone begin with ph.

mcqs.q: Which word has 'th' at the beginning?
mcqs.why: Thumb begins with the digraph th; teeth and mouth end with th, and sing ends with ng.

mcqs.q: Which word has 'th' at the ending?
mcqs.why: Teeth ends with the digraph th, while thumb and thick begin with th.

mcqs.q: Which word ends with the digraph 'ng'?
mcqs.why: King ends with the digraph ng; graph ends with ph and cloth and path end with th.

mcqs.q: Can an English word begin with 'ng'?
mcqs.why: There is no word beginning with the ng sound or digraph in the English language; ng comes at the end of words like king and ring.

mcqs.q: Which word completes 'dol____in'?
mcqs.why: Adding ph to dol____in makes the word dolphin, an animal that lives in the sea.

mcqs.q: The word 'three' begins with which digraph?
mcqs.why: Three begins with the letters th, which together make one sound, so th is its digraph.

lessons.title: 1.3.2 Use of Ending Punctuations
lessons.notes_html:
Full Stop

  • A full stop (.) is used at the end of a simple sentence.
  • I am in class two.
  • He is my best friend.
  • She is my little sister.

Question Mark

  • A question mark (?) is used at the end of a question.
  • What is in your hands?
  • Who is your class teacher?
  • What games do you like?

Key Points

  • Simple sentences end with a full stop.
  • Questions end with a question mark.

mcqs.q: The sentence 'I am in class two' ends with a:
mcqs.why: It is a simple sentence, and simple sentences end with a full stop.

mcqs.q: The sentence 'What is in your hands' ends with a:
mcqs.why: It asks something, and questions end with a question mark at the end.

mcqs.q: Which sentence has the correct punctuation?
mcqs.why: A simple telling sentence ends with a full stop, so 'My name is Ali.' is correct.

mcqs.q: 'Who is your class teacher' is a:
mcqs.why: It asks who the teacher is, so it is a question and needs a question mark.

mcqs.q: Which ending is correct for 'He is my best friend'?
mcqs.why: It is a simple sentence about a friend, so it ends with a full stop.

mcqs.q: Which ending is correct for 'Are you Abbas'?
mcqs.why: It asks a question, so it must end with a question mark, not a full stop.

mcqs.q: 'She is my little sister' needs which mark at the end?
mcqs.why: The sentence tells something about the sister, so it ends with a full stop.

mcqs.q: 'What games do you like' needs which mark at the end?
mcqs.why: The sentence asks about games, so it ends with a question mark.

mcqs.q: Is this correct: 'Is Maryum five years old.'?
options: No, a question needs a question mark
Yes, full stops end all sentences
mcqs.why: The sentence asks about Maryum's age, so it needs a question mark at the end, not a full stop.

mcqs.q: A question always ends with a:
mcqs.why: Every question ends with a question mark; that is the rule of ending punctuation in this lesson.

lessons.title: 1.4.1 Objects in a Picture
lessons.notes_html:
Objects in the Park Picture

In the big picture, children are playing in a park in front of their school. The numbered objects in the picture are:

lessons.title: 1.4.2 Answer the Questions
lessons.notes_html:
Talking About Myself

  • What class are you in? I am in class two.
  • Who is your best friend? My best friend is Amjad. He is kind and we play together.
  • What is your age? I am seven years old.
  • Who is your teacher? My teacher is Miss Shazia. She teaches us English and she is very kind.

Practice Note

This is a speaking and writing practice lesson. Answer the questions about yourself in simple sentences, like the model answers.

Key Points

  • We answer questions about ourselves in simple, complete sentences.
  • Every answer sentence begins with a capital letter and ends with a full stop.

lessons.title: 2.1 Introducing Pets
lessons.notes_html:
Alia's Pets

  • Alia says: Hello, Azan. Meet my pets.
  • Azan says: Hello, Alia. Your pets are cute.
  • Alia likes cats and birds. She has a cat and a parrot at home.
  • Her cat is Kheeri and her parrot is Chenu.

Azan's Pet

This is a speaking-practice dialogue. Practise it in pairs with a class fellow.

lessons.title: 2.2 Alia's Pets
lessons.notes_html:
Alia's Three Pets

  • Alia has three pets: Kheeri the cat, Chenu the parrot and Moti the dog.
  • Alia takes care of her pets.

Kheeri the Cat

  • Kheeri has soft white fur.
  • Kheeri likes milk and fish and says 'meow meow'.

Chenu the Parrot

  • Chenu has green feathers and a red beak.
  • Chenu eats guava and chillies and rests in its big cage.

Moti the Dog

  • Moti is a brown fluffy dog.
  • Alia gives Moti biscuits and milk. Moti says 'boww boww'.

Domestic and Wild Animals

  • Domestic animals live with humans: cow, buffalo, goat, donkey, cat and horse.
  • Wild animals live in jungles: lion, tiger, elephant, giraffe, bear and deer.

Word Families

  • beak, peak, speak, weak, leak end with the sound 'eak'.
  • brown, town, crown, down end with the sound 'own'.
  • take, make, fake, lake, snake end with the sound 'ake'.

Key Points

  • We should take care of our pets and give them food.
  • Domestic animals live with us; wild animals live in jungles.

mcqs.why: Alia has three pets: Kheeri the cat, Chenu the parrot and Moti the dog.

mcqs.q: Alia gives biscuits and milk to:
mcqs.why: Alia gives biscuits and milk to Moti the dog, who says 'boww boww'.

lessons.title: 2.3.1 Proper Nouns
lessons.notes_html:
Proper Nouns

  • A proper noun is the particular name of any person, place, animal or thing.
  • Proper nouns begin with a capital letter.
  • Examples: Amjad (person), Chenu (parrot), Hyderabad City Park (place) and My English Book Two (thing).

Common and Proper Nouns

  • girl : Kashaf; boy : Zain; airport : Jinnah International Airport
  • city : Karachi; person : Wahab; cat : Kheeri

Key Points

  • Common nouns are common names; proper nouns are particular names.
  • Names of days and cities are also proper nouns, like Monday and Larkana.

mcqs.q: A proper noun is the ____ name of a person, place, animal or thing.
mcqs.why: A proper noun is the particular name of any person, place, animal or thing, like Amjad or Karachi.

mcqs.q: Proper nouns begin with a:
mcqs.why: Proper nouns begin with a capital letter, for example Chenu and Hyderabad City Park.

mcqs.q: Which word is a proper noun?
mcqs.why: Karachi is the particular name of a city, so it is a proper noun; city, girl and cat are common nouns.

mcqs.q: Which word is a proper noun?
mcqs.why: Kheeri is the particular name of one cat, so it is a proper noun; cat, pet and animal are common names.

mcqs.q: The proper noun for 'city' in the lesson is:
mcqs.why: In the lesson, the common noun city is matched with the proper noun Karachi.

mcqs.q: 'Monday' is a proper noun because it is the name of a:
mcqs.why: Monday is the particular name of a day, so it begins with a capital letter as a proper noun.

mcqs.q: In 'Dr. Aslam is a kind doctor', the proper noun is:
mcqs.why: Dr. Aslam is the particular name of the doctor, so it is the proper noun in the sentence.

mcqs.q: Names of pets like Kheeri and Moti are:
mcqs.why: Names of pets are particular names, so Kheeri and Moti are proper nouns and begin with capital letters.

mcqs.q: 'Hyderabad City Park' is the proper name of a:
mcqs.why: Hyderabad City Park is given in the lesson as the proper name of a place.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a common noun?
mcqs.why: Girl is a common name for any girl, while Kashaf, Zain and Karachi are particular names.

lessons.title: 2.3.2 Making Plurals
lessons.notes_html:
Rule One: Add -s

  • Most naming words are made plural by adding '-s' at the end.
  • cat : cats, book : books, chair : chairs, cup : cups, bottle : bottles, tree : trees.

Rule Two: Add -es

  • Words ending with -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -o, -x are made plural by adding '-es' at the end.
  • bus : buses, glass : glasses, brush : brushes, watch : watches, tomato : tomatoes, box : boxes.

Key Points

  • Add -s to most words to make them plural.
  • Add -es to words ending in -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -o or -x.

mcqs.q: Most words are made plural by adding:
mcqs.why: Rule One says most common naming words are made plural by adding -s at the end, like cats and books.

mcqs.q: Words ending in -sh, -ch or -x are made plural by adding:
mcqs.why: Rule Two says words ending with -s, -ss, -sh, -ch, -o or -x take -es, like brushes, watches and boxes.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'cat'?
mcqs.why: Cat does not end with a Rule Two ending, so we add only -s and get cats.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'bus'?
mcqs.why: Bus ends with -s, so we add -es to make the plural buses.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'watch'?
mcqs.why: Watch ends with -ch, so we add -es and make the plural watches.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'tomato'?
mcqs.why: Tomato ends with -o, so we add -es to make the plural tomatoes.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'box'?
mcqs.why: Box ends with -x, so we add -es and get the plural boxes.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'chair'?
mcqs.why: Chair takes only -s by Rule One, so its plural is chairs.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'brush'?
mcqs.why: Brush ends with -sh, so we add -es and make the plural brushes.

mcqs.q: What is the plural of 'potato'?
mcqs.why: Potato ends with -o like tomato, so we add -es and get potatoes.

lessons.title: 2.3.3 Ending Sounds in Plurals
lessons.notes_html:
Three Ending Sounds

  • Plural words can end with the sounds /s/, /z/ or /iz/.
  • /s/ sound: tents, cups, pots, desks. Also cats, books, goats and cups.
  • /z/ sound: boys, fans, girls, bells. Also bags, pens, dogs and kettles.
  • /iz/ sound: wishes, trashes, brushes, boxes. Also buses, watches, foxes and dishes.

Key Points

  • Words with -s, -sh, -ch or -x endings take the /iz/ ending sound in their plurals.
  • Listen to the last sound of a plural word to find its group.

mcqs.q: The plural word 'cups' ends with the sound:
mcqs.why: Cups is in the /s/ group of the lesson table, with tents, pots and desks.

mcqs.q: The plural word 'boys' ends with the sound:
mcqs.why: Boys ends with the /z/ sound, like fans, girls and bells in the lesson table.

mcqs.q: The plural word 'wishes' ends with the sound:
mcqs.why: Wishes ends with the /iz/ sound, like trashes, brushes and boxes.

mcqs.q: Which word ends with the /s/ sound?
mcqs.why: Desks ends with /s/; boys and girls end with /z/, and boxes ends with /iz/.

mcqs.q: Which word ends with the /z/ sound?
mcqs.why: Bells ends with /z/; cups and pots end with /s/, and wishes ends with /iz/.

mcqs.q: Which word ends with the /iz/ sound?
mcqs.why: Brushes ends with /iz/ because brush ends with -sh; tents and desks end with /s/ and fans with /z/.

mcqs.q: The plural word 'dogs' ends with the sound:
mcqs.why: In the lesson table, dogs is placed in the /z/ group with bags, pens and kettles.

mcqs.q: The plural word 'buses' ends with the sound:
mcqs.why: Buses ends with /iz/, like watches, foxes and dishes in the lesson table.

mcqs.q: The plural word 'books' ends with the sound:
mcqs.why: Books is in the /s/ group of the lesson table, with cats, goats and cups.

mcqs.q: How many ending sounds do plural words have in this lesson?
mcqs.why: The lesson sorts plurals into three ending sounds: /s/, /z/ and /iz/.

lessons.title: 2.3.4 Use of 'These' and 'Those'
lessons.notes_html:
These

  • These + are is used to point to many things near the speaker.
  • Examples: These are bags. These are cats. These are buses.

Those

  • Those + are is used to point to many things away from the speaker.
  • Examples: Those are bags. Those are trees. Those are tomatoes.

Key Points

  • Use 'these' for things near you and 'those' for things far from you.
  • Both 'these' and 'those' are used with 'are' for more than one thing.

mcqs.q: We use 'these' for many things that are:
mcqs.why: These + are points to many things near the speaker, like 'These are bags.'

mcqs.q: We use 'those' for many things that are:
mcqs.why: Those + are points to many things away from the speaker, like 'Those are bags.'

mcqs.q: The cats are near the girl. Complete: '____ are cats.'
mcqs.why: The cats are near the girl, so we use 'these': These are cats.

mcqs.q: The trees are far away from the girl. Complete: '____ are trees.'
mcqs.why: The trees are away from the speaker, so we use 'those': Those are trees.

mcqs.q: The boy is standing near two buses. Complete: '____ are buses.'
mcqs.why: The buses are near the boy, so we say 'These are buses.'

mcqs.q: The tomatoes are far away from the boy. Complete: '____ are tomatoes.'
mcqs.why: The tomatoes are away from the speaker, so we say 'Those are tomatoes.'

mcqs.q: 'These' and 'those' are used with the word:
mcqs.why: The lesson uses 'These are' and 'Those are' because we point to more than one thing.

mcqs.q: Which sentence points to things near the speaker?
mcqs.why: 'These are bags' points to many bags near the speaker; 'those' points to bags far away.

mcqs.q: Which sentence points to things far away?
mcqs.why: 'Those are trees' points to trees away from the speaker, as in the lesson pictures.

mcqs.q: 'These' and 'those' are used for:
mcqs.why: Both words point to many things, so they are used for more than one thing with 'are'.

lessons.title: 2.4.1 One Syllable and Two Syllable Words
lessons.notes_html:
What is a Syllable?

  • A syllable is a part of a word that contains a single vowel sound.
  • One-syllable words have one clap; two-syllable words have two claps.

One Syllable Words

  • car, pen, ball, bus, sun, boy, bulb, tree, moon.

Two Syllable Words

  • Khee-ri, ki-tchen, gua-va, mon-key, pi-geon, pill-ow, wa-ter, bis-cuit, par-rot.

Key Points

  • Clap once for each syllable as you say a word to count its syllables.

mcqs.q: A syllable is a part of a word that contains a single ____ sound.
mcqs.why: A syllable is a part of a word that contains a single vowel sound, as the lesson explains.

mcqs.q: How many syllables are in the word 'car'?
mcqs.why: Car has one syllable and one clap, like pen, ball and sun.

mcqs.q: The word 'kitchen' has:
mcqs.why: Kitchen breaks into ki-tchen, so it has two syllables and two claps.

mcqs.q: Which word has one syllable?
mcqs.why: Pen has one syllable; monkey, water and parrot each have two syllables.

mcqs.q: Which word has two syllables?
mcqs.why: Guava breaks into gua-va, so it has two syllables; ball, sun and tree have one each.

mcqs.q: The word 'pigeon' breaks into:
mcqs.why: Pigeon breaks into two parts, pi-geon, so it is a two-syllable word.

mcqs.q: One-syllable words have how many claps?
mcqs.why: One-syllable words have one clap and two-syllable words have two claps.

mcqs.q: The word 'biscuit' has:
mcqs.why: Biscuit breaks into bis-cuit, which makes two syllables.

mcqs.q: Which is a two-syllable word?
mcqs.why: Pillow breaks into pill-ow, so it has two syllables; bus, moon and boy have one each.

mcqs.q: The word 'parrot' breaks into:
mcqs.why: Parrot breaks into par-rot, two syllables, as shown in the lesson word list.

lessons.title: 3.1 Sharing Daily Routine
lessons.notes_html:
Evening Routine

  • The teacher asks: Students, tell me what do you do daily in the evening?
  • Bilal does his homework at 5:30 in the evening. He does his homework first in the evening.
  • Kiran helps her mother in small chores. She is a helpful girl.
  • Asma goes to play with friends at 6:30 in the evening.
  • At the end the teacher says: Good answers, everyone! Well done!

Practice Note

This is a speaking-practice dialogue. Practise it in groups and tell the class about your own evening routine.

Key Points

  • We do our homework on time and help our parents in small chores.
  • Playing with friends in the evening is also part of a good daily routine.

mcqs.q: What does Bilal do at 5:30 in the evening?
mcqs.why: Bilal answers, 'Teacher, I do my homework on 5:30 in the evening,' and he does it first.

mcqs.q: Who helps her mother in small chores?
mcqs.why: Kiran helps her mother in small chores in the evening, and she is a helpful girl.

mcqs.q: What does Asma do at 6:30 in the evening?
options: She goes to play with friends
mcqs.why: Asma goes to play with friends on 6:30 in the evening, as she tells the teacher.

mcqs.q: Kiran is a ____ girl.
mcqs.why: Kiran helps her mother in small chores, so the lesson calls her a helpful girl.

mcqs.q: Who asks the students about their daily routine?
mcqs.why: The teacher asks, 'Students, tell me what do you do daily in the evening?'

mcqs.q: What does the teacher say at the end?
mcqs.why: At the end the teacher praises the class: 'Good answers, everyone! Well done!'

mcqs.q: Bilal does his homework ____ in the evening.
mcqs.why: Bilal does his homework first in the evening, before other things.

mcqs.q: At what time does Bilal do his homework?
mcqs.why: Bilal does his homework on 5:30 in the evening; Asma plays at 6:30.

mcqs.q: At what time does Asma go to play?
mcqs.why: Asma goes to play with friends on 6:30 in the evening.

mcqs.q: Helping parents in small chores is a:
mcqs.why: Helping parents at home in small chores is a good habit, and everyone loves such children.

lessons.title: 3.2 Helping in Small Chores
lessons.notes_html:
Ahmed Goes to the Market

  • Ahmed and his mother go to the market at 10:30 in the morning on the weekend.
  • First, they buy pencils, colour markers, erasers and sharpeners from a stationery shop.
  • Second, they buy apples, bananas and oranges from a fruit shop.
  • Third, they buy tomatoes, potatoes and carrots from a vegetable shop.
  • They return home at 12:30 at noon.

Ahmed Helps at Home

  • Fourth, Ahmed helps his mother in small chores: he washes dishes and cleans the dining table.
  • Fifth, Ahmed helps his brother in homework.
  • Everyone loves Ahmed for his good manners.

Shops and Things

  • We buy fruits from a fruit shop, vegetables from a vegetable shop, stationery from a stationery shop, toys from a toys shop and cloth from a cloth shop.

Key Points

  • We should help our parents at home in small chores.
  • Different shops sell different things.

mcqs.q: Where does Ahmed go with his mother on the weekend?
mcqs.why: Ahmed goes to the market with his mother on the weekend, at 10:30 in the morning.

mcqs.q: At what time do Ahmed and his mother go to the market?
mcqs.why: They go to market on 10:30 in the morning and return home on 12:30 at noon.

mcqs.q: What do they buy first?
mcqs.why: First, Ahmed and his mother buy pencils, colour markers, erasers and sharpeners from a stationery shop.

mcqs.q: From which shop do they buy pencils and erasers?
mcqs.why: Pencils, colour markers, erasers and sharpeners are bought from a stationery shop.

mcqs.q: Which fruits do they buy?
mcqs.why: They buy apples, bananas and oranges from a fruit shop; these fruits are fresh and sweet.

mcqs.q: Which vegetables do they buy?
mcqs.why: They buy tomatoes, potatoes and carrots from a vegetable shop.

mcqs.q: How does Ahmed help his mother in small chores?
options: He washes dishes and cleans the dining table
mcqs.why: Ahmed washes dishes and cleans the dining table to help his mother in small chores.

mcqs.q: Who does Ahmed help in homework?
mcqs.why: Fifth, Ahmed helps his brother in homework, and everyone loves him for his good manners.

mcqs.q: At what time do Ahmed and his mother return home?
mcqs.why: Ahmed and his mother return home on 12:30 at noon after shopping.

mcqs.q: Why does everyone love Ahmed?
mcqs.why: Everyone loves Ahmed for his good manners because he always helps his family members.

lessons.title: 3.2.1 Understanding the Time (in Half Hour)
lessons.notes_html:
Half Past

  • When the minute hand is on 6, it is half past the hour.
  • 7:30 is read as Half past seven.
  • The short hand is the hour hand; the long hand is the minute hand.
  • For half past, the hour hand is between two numbers.

Times in My Day

  • I wake up at 7:30. I have school break at 11:30.
  • I come back home at 1:30. I play in the evening at 6:30.
  • I have dinner at 9:30. I go to bed at 10:30.

Key Points

  • Minute hand on 6 and the hour hand just past a number means half past that hour.

mcqs.q: When the minute hand is on 6, the time is:
mcqs.why: When the minute hand is on 6, it is half past the hour, like 7:30, half past seven.

mcqs.q: 7:30 in words is:
mcqs.why: The time 7:30 is written in words as 'Half past seven' in the lesson.

mcqs.q: The long hand of a clock is the:
mcqs.why: The long hand is the minute hand and the short hand is the hour hand on a clock.

mcqs.q: To draw 12:30, the hour hand is drawn between:
mcqs.why: For half past 12, draw the minute hand on 6 and the hour hand between 12 and 1.

mcqs.q: In the lesson matching, 'I wake up at ____.'
mcqs.why: 'I wake up at 7:30' matches the clock showing half past seven.

mcqs.q: In the lesson matching, the school break is at:
mcqs.why: 'I have school break at 11:30' matches the clock showing half past eleven.

mcqs.q: In the lesson matching, dinner time is:
mcqs.why: 'I have dinner at 9:30' matches the clock showing half past nine.

mcqs.q: In the lesson matching, bed time is:
mcqs.why: 'I go to bed at 10:30' matches the clock showing half past ten.

mcqs.q: To draw 4:30 on a clock, the minute hand is drawn on:
mcqs.why: For every half past time, the long minute hand is drawn on 6 and the hour hand between the two numbers.

mcqs.q: 'Half past twelve' in numbers is:
mcqs.why: Half past twelve means thirty minutes past twelve, which is written as 12:30.

lessons.title: 3.3.1 Use of Capitalization
lessons.notes_html:
Capital Letters

  • The first word of every sentence begins with a capital letter.
  • Names of persons and animals begin with capital letters: Alia, Moti, Kashaf, Bushra, Saba.
  • Statements end with a full stop; questions end with a question mark.

Correct Sentences

  • Alia plays with Moti in the park.
  • Kashaf, Bushra, and Saba are friends.
  • Where is your school?
  • What is in your bag?

Key Points

  • Always begin a sentence and a name with a capital letter.

mcqs.q: Which word of a sentence must begin with a capital letter?
mcqs.why: The first word of a sentence begins with a capital letter, and so do the names of persons and animals.

mcqs.q: Names of persons begin with:
mcqs.why: Names of persons and animals like Alia and Moti begin with capital letters.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: Alia plays with moti in the garden.
Alia play with Moti in the park.
alia plays with moti in the park
Alia plays with Moti in the park.
mcqs.why: Both the first word Alia and the pet's name Moti need capital letters, and the sentence ends with a full stop.

mcqs.q: The correct form of 'where is your school' is:
mcqs.why: The first word begins with a capital letter and the question ends with a question mark.

mcqs.q: In 'kashaf, bushra, and saba are friends', which words get capital letters?
mcqs.why: Kashaf, Bushra and Saba are names of persons, so all three begin with capital letters.

mcqs.q: A statement ends with a:
mcqs.why: Statements end with a full stop, while questions end with a question mark.

mcqs.q: A question ends with a:
mcqs.why: Questions like 'What is in your bag?' end with a question mark.

mcqs.q: In 'What is in your bag?', the word with the capital letter is:
mcqs.why: What is the first word of the question, so it begins with a capital letter.

mcqs.q: The name of a pet like Moti begins with a:
mcqs.why: Names of animals also begin with capital letters, like Moti the pet in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Which sentence is written correctly?
options: kashaf, bushra, and saba are friend.
Kashaf, bushra, and saba are friends
Kashaf, Bushra, and Saba are friends.
Kashaf, Bushra, and Saba are good friends.
mcqs.why: All three names begin with capital letters and the sentence ends with a full stop; the last option adds a word that is not in the lesson sentence.

lessons.title: 3.3.2 Describing Words
lessons.notes_html:
Describing Words

  • A describing word tells us more about a person or a thing.
  • intelligent (student), red (flower), new (book), big (house), fresh (vegetables), clean (water).

Describing Pictures

  • It is a red ball. It is a blue car. It is a yummy cake. It is a green frog.
  • It is a big elephant. It is a dirty shirt. He is an angry man. He is a happy boy.

Opposite Describing Words

  • sad : happy, big : small, long : short, hot : cold, white : black.

Key Points

  • Describing words come before the person or thing they describe.
  • Colour words like red, yellow, white and black are also describing words.

mcqs.q: A describing word tells us more about a:
mcqs.why: A describing word describes a naming word, that is, a person or a thing, like 'intelligent student'.

mcqs.q: In 'Ahmed is an intelligent student', the describing word is:
mcqs.why: The word 'intelligent' describes the student Ahmed, so it is the describing word.

mcqs.q: In 'She smells a red flower', the word 'red' describes the:
mcqs.why: Red describes the flower; colour words are describing words in this lesson.

mcqs.q: In 'He lives in a big house', the describing word is:
mcqs.why: Big describes the house, so 'big' is the describing word in the sentence.

mcqs.q: In 'They buy fresh vegetables', the describing word is:
mcqs.why: Fresh describes the vegetables, so 'fresh' is the describing word.

mcqs.q: In 'It is a dirty shirt', the describing word is:
mcqs.why: Dirty describes the shirt in the picture sentence, so it is the describing word.

mcqs.q: What is the opposite of 'happy'?
mcqs.why: Sad and happy are opposite describing words, as in the sad boy and the happy girl.

mcqs.q: What is the opposite of 'big'?
mcqs.why: Big and small are opposite describing words, like the big house and the small house.

mcqs.q: Complete the pair: Fire is ____ and ice is ____.
mcqs.why: The lesson sentences are 'Fire is hot' and 'Ice is cold'; hot and cold are opposites.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a colour describing word?
mcqs.why: Yellow is a colour describing word, as in 'It is a yellow flower' in the lesson.

lessons.title: 3.3.4 Use of Plural Pronouns (Subjects)
lessons.notes_html:
Plural Pronouns with 'are'

  • We, You and They are plural pronouns. They are used with 'are'.
  • We are brave girls. You are players of cricket. They are best friends.

Who Does the Pronoun Stand For?

  • I : Rafiq, the father, who works in a factory.
  • She : Mrs. Salma Rafiq, a teacher, the mother of Areeba and Abbas.
  • We : Mr. and Mrs. Rafiq. 'We have two children, Areeba and Abbas.' 'We are a happy family.'
  • They : Areeba and Abbas, who go to school in the morning.
  • It : Kheeri, Areeba's pet cat.
  • You : Areeba and Abbas. 'You are good students.'

Key Points

  • Use We, You and They with 'are' when we talk about more than one person.

mcqs.q: Complete: '____ are brave girls.'
mcqs.why: 'We are brave girls' is correct because 'we' is used with 'are' for more than one person.

mcqs.q: Complete: '____ are players of cricket.'
mcqs.why: 'You are players of cricket' is correct; 'you' is a plural pronoun used with 'are' here.

mcqs.q: Complete: '____ are best friends.'
mcqs.why: 'They are best friends' is correct because 'they' is used for many persons who are not with the speaker.

mcqs.q: In the family passage, 'I am Rafiq' : 'I' stands for:
mcqs.why: In line 1, 'I' is Rafiq, the father, who works in a factory.

mcqs.q: Rafiq works in a:
mcqs.why: Rafiq says, 'I work in a factory,' so he works in a factory.

mcqs.q: In the family passage, 'She is Mrs. Salma Rafiq' : 'She' stands for:
mcqs.why: 'She' is Mrs. Salma Rafiq, a teacher and the mother of Areeba and Abbas.

mcqs.q: Mrs. Salma Rafiq is a:
mcqs.why: Mrs. Salma Rafiq is a teacher, as the family passage tells us.

mcqs.q: 'We have two children' : the two children are:
mcqs.why: Mr. and Mrs. Rafiq have two children, Areeba and Abbas, who go to school in the morning.

mcqs.q: 'It is her pet cat' : 'It' stands for:
mcqs.why: 'It' is Kheeri, Areeba's pet cat, with whom Areeba plays.

mcqs.q: Which pronoun is used with 'are' for many people who are not with us?
mcqs.why: 'They' is used for many persons who are not with the speaker, as in 'They are best friends.'

lessons.title: 3.4.1 Writing List of Items
lessons.notes_html:
Lists from the Passage

  • Stationery: pencils, colour markers, erasers, sharpeners.
  • Fruits: apples, bananas, oranges.
  • Vegetables: tomatoes, potatoes, carrots.

Action Words and Syllables

  • Action words show some action happening.
  • Two-syllable action words in the lesson: going and helping.
  • Three-syllable action words: providing and answering.

Key Points

  • We write the names of things in separate lists under their groups.

mcqs.q: Which list has only stationery items?
mcqs.why: The stationery list from the passage has pencils, colour markers, erasers and sharpeners.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a fruit in the passage list?
mcqs.why: Banana is in the fruits list with apples and oranges; carrot and tomato are vegetables.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a vegetable in the passage list?
mcqs.why: Potato is in the vegetables list with tomatoes and carrots.

mcqs.q: The action word 'going' has how many syllables?
mcqs.why: 'Going' and 'helping' are the two-syllable action words given in the lesson.

mcqs.q: The action word 'helping' is a:
mcqs.why: Helping is a two-syllable action word, as in 'Ahmed is helping his mother.'

mcqs.q: The action word 'providing' has:
mcqs.why: 'Providing' and 'answering' are three-syllable action words in the lesson.

mcqs.q: The action word 'answering' has:
mcqs.why: Answering has three syllables, as in 'Areeba is answering a question.'

mcqs.q: Action words show:
mcqs.why: Action words show some action happening, like going, helping and answering.

mcqs.q: Complete the lesson sentence: 'Kashaf is ____ water to her mother.'
mcqs.why: The lesson sentence is 'Kashaf is providing water to her mother,' using the action word providing.

mcqs.q: Sharpeners belong to which list?
mcqs.why: Sharpeners are in the stationery list with pencils, colour markers and erasers.

lessons.title: 3.4.2 Action Words
lessons.notes_html:
Action Words from the Box

  • The baby is crying loudly. They are running in the race.
  • She is completing her homework. Asma is watering the plants.
  • Waheeda is throwing a ball. Kashaf is catching a ball.
  • We are celebrating 14th August. Wahab is colouring the drawing.

Ahmed's Daily Actions

  • He wakes up early in the morning. He brushes his teeth daily.
  • He eats breakfast and goes to school daily.
  • He plays with friends in the evening, completes his homework at night and goes to bed early at night.

Key Points

  • Action words tell what someone is doing.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'The baby is ____ loudly.'
mcqs.why: The picture of the crying baby completes the sentence: 'The baby is crying loudly.'

mcqs.q: Complete: 'They are ____ in the race.'
mcqs.why: They are running in the race; running is the action word from the box for this sentence.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'She is ____ her homework.'
mcqs.why: She is completing her homework; 'completing' is the action word that fits homework.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Asma is ____ the plants.'
mcqs.why: Asma is watering the plants; we water plants to help them grow.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Waheeda is ____ a ball.'
mcqs.why: Waheeda is throwing a ball, while Kashaf is catching a ball.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Kashaf is ____ a ball.'
mcqs.why: Kashaf is catching a ball; catching is the opposite action of throwing here.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'We are ____ 14th August.'
mcqs.why: We are celebrating 14th August, the Independence Day of Pakistan.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Wahab is ____ the drawing.'
mcqs.why: Wahab is colouring the drawing with colours.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Ahmed ____ his teeth daily.'
mcqs.why: Ahmed brushes his teeth daily; it is one of his daily actions in the lesson.

mcqs.q: Complete: 'Ahmed ____ his homework at night daily.'
mcqs.why: Ahmed completes his homework at night and goes to bed early at night.

lessons.title: 3.4.3 Use of Ordinal Numbers
lessons.notes_html:
Cardinal and Ordinal Numbers

  • Cardinal numbers show how many things there are in total.
  • Ordinal numbers show the position of a thing in a sequence.
  • one : first, two : second, three : third, four : fourth, five : fifth
  • six : sixth, seven : seventh, eight : eighth, nine : ninth, ten : tenth

Examples

  • The first dog is white. The second frog is green. The third butterfly is purple.
  • The fourth chair is blue. The sixth flower is yellow. The seventh pen is red. The eighth cat is black. The tenth apple is red.

Key Points

  • Use ordinal numbers to tell the position of a thing: first, second, third and so on.

mcqs.q: Ordinal numbers show the ____ of a thing.
mcqs.why: Ordinal numbers show the position of an object in a sequence, like first, second and third.

mcqs.q: The ordinal number for 'one' is:
mcqs.why: One : first. The ordinal of one is first, as in 'The first dog is white.'

mcqs.q: The ordinal number for 'two' is:
mcqs.why: Two : second, as in 'The second frog is green' in the lesson activity.

mcqs.q: The ordinal number for 'three' is:
mcqs.why: Three : third, as in 'The third butterfly is purple.'

mcqs.q: The ordinal number for 'five' is:
mcqs.why: Five : fifth; the ordinal numbers from one to ten are learned in this lesson.

mcqs.q: The ordinal number for 'eight' is:
mcqs.why: Eight : eighth, as in 'The eighth cat is black' in the lesson.

mcqs.q: The ordinal number for 'ten' is:
mcqs.why: Ten : tenth, as in 'The tenth fruit is a red apple.'

mcqs.q: Two frogs are shown. Complete: 'The ____ frog is green.'
mcqs.why: The first frog is yellow and the second frog is green, so the answer is second.

mcqs.q: Four chairs are shown. Complete: 'The ____ chair is blue.'
mcqs.why: These are four chairs and the fourth chair is blue, as the lesson activity says.

mcqs.q: Cardinal numbers show:
options: how many things there are in total
mcqs.why: Cardinal numbers show total digits, while ordinal numbers show the position of an object in a sequence.

lessons.title: 4.1 Talking about Seasons
lessons.notes_html:
Favourite Seasons

  • Anjali likes winter because she wears warm clothes and drinks hot soup.
  • Kashaf likes spring because flowers bloom and the weather is nice. Spring makes everyone happy.

Seasons We Do Not Like

  • Mohan does not like summer because it is too hot to play outside in the day time.
  • Zain does not like winter because he gets flu all the time.

Practice Note

This is a speaking-practice dialogue. Practise it in pairs or groups and talk about the season you like.

Key Points

  • There are four seasons in a year: spring, summer, autumn and winter.
  • We can tell the season we like and the reason for it.

mcqs.q: Which season does Anjali like?
mcqs.why: Anjali says, 'Kashaf, I like winter because I wear warm clothes and drink hot soup.'

mcqs.q: Why does Anjali like winter?
options: She wears warm clothes and drinks hot soup
mcqs.why: Anjali likes winter because she wears warm clothes and drinks hot soup in it.

mcqs.q: Which season does Kashaf like?
mcqs.why: Kashaf likes spring because flowers bloom and the weather is nice.

mcqs.q: Why does Kashaf like spring?
options: Flowers bloom and the weather is nice
mcqs.why: Kashaf likes spring because flowers bloom and the weather is nice; spring makes everyone happy.

mcqs.q: Which season does Mohan not like?
mcqs.why: Mohan says, 'Zain, I do not like summer because it is too hot to play outside.'

mcqs.q: Why does Mohan not like summer?
options: It is too hot to play outside in the day time
mcqs.why: Mohan does not like summer because it is too hot to play outside in the day time.

mcqs.q: Which season does Zain not like?
mcqs.why: Zain does not like winter because he gets flu all the time in winter.

mcqs.q: Why does Zain not like winter?
options: He gets flu all the time
mcqs.why: Zain does not like winter because he often falls sick with flu in winter.

mcqs.q: Spring makes everyone:
mcqs.why: The lesson says spring makes everyone happy because flowers bloom and the weather is nice.

mcqs.q: Zain gets ____ in winter.
mcqs.why: Zain gets flu all the time in winter, so he does not like the winter season.

lessons.title: 4.2 Seasons (Nursery Rhyme)
lessons.notes_html:
The Four Seasons

  • There are four seasons in a year: spring, summer, autumn and winter.
  • There are twelve months in a year.
  • We have summer vacations in June and July, and winter vacations in December.

What the Poem Says

  • Spring: flowers bloom and all are happy, no one glooms.
  • Summer: bright sunshine and hot wind; rain delights us.
  • Autumn: yellow leaves fall down; they are dry, crunchy and brown.
  • Winter: cold mornings and icy air; we sip hot tea and wear warm sweaters.

Key Points

  • Warm clothes are worn in winter, not in summer.
  • In the poem, we enjoy the rain in summer.

mcqs.q: How many seasons are there in a year?
mcqs.why: There are four seasons in a year: spring, summer, autumn and winter.

mcqs.q: How many months are there in a year?
mcqs.why: There are twelve months in a year, from January to December.

mcqs.q: In which season do flowers bloom?
mcqs.why: The poem says, 'In spring, flowers bloom,' and all are happy in spring.

mcqs.q: In summer, ____ shines bright.
mcqs.why: The poem's MCQ tells us that in summer the sun shines bright.

mcqs.q: In which season do leaves turn yellow and fall?
mcqs.why: In autumn, yellow leaves fall down; they are dry, crunchy and brown.

mcqs.q: We sip ____ in the winter season.
mcqs.why: The poem says we sip hot tea and wear warm sweaters in winter.

mcqs.q: In which season do we enjoy the rain, according to the poem?
mcqs.why: The poem says we enjoy rain in summer, not in winter.

mcqs.q: Summer vacations are in the months of:
mcqs.why: We have summer vacations in the hot months of June and July.

mcqs.q: Winter vacations are in the month of:
mcqs.why: We have winter vacations in December when it is very cold.

mcqs.q: In winter we wear:
mcqs.why: The poem says we wear warm sweaters in winter with its cold mornings and icy air.

lessons.title: 4.2.1 Months in a Year
lessons.notes_html:
Days in the Months

  • Months with thirty days: April, June, September and November.
  • Months with thirty-one days: January, March, May, July, August, October and December. There are seven such months.
  • February has twenty-eight days. In a leap year, February has twenty-nine days and the year has 366 days.

Order of the Months

  • First month: January. Fourth: April. Seventh: July. Ninth: September. Last month: December.
  • Months starting with 'J': January, June, July. With 'A': April, August. With 'M': March, May.

Seasons and Months (from the book)

  • Spring comes in February, March and April. Summer comes in May, June and July.
  • Autumn comes in August, September and October. Winter comes in November, December and January.

Key Points

  • February is the month which makes a leap year.

mcqs.q: Which month has twenty-eight days?
mcqs.why: February is the month with twenty-eight days; in a leap year it has twenty-nine days.

mcqs.q: In a leap year, February has:
mcqs.why: In a leap year February has 29 days instead of 28, so the year has 366 days.

mcqs.q: Which of these months has thirty days?
mcqs.why: April, June, September and November have thirty days each; January, March and December have thirty-one.

mcqs.q: How many months have thirty-one days?
mcqs.why: January, March, May, July, August, October and December are the seven months with thirty-one days.

mcqs.q: The first month of the year is:
mcqs.why: The first month of the year is January and the last month is December.

mcqs.q: The last month of the year is:
mcqs.why: December is the last, twelfth month of the year.

mcqs.q: The seventh month of the year is:
mcqs.why: Counting the months, the seventh month of the year is July.

mcqs.q: The ninth month of the year is:
mcqs.why: The ninth month of the year is September, as the calendar activity tells us.

mcqs.q: Which months start with the letter 'J'?
mcqs.why: The months starting with J are January, June and July.

mcqs.q: A leap year has how many days in total?
mcqs.why: In a leap year February has 29 days, so the whole year has 366 days.

lessons.title: 4.3.1 Opposite Describing Words
lessons.notes_html:
Opposite Pairs

  • small : big, full : empty, young : old
  • hot : cold, slow : fast, day : night

Key Points

lessons.title: 4.3.2 Use of Apostrophe
lessons.notes_html:
Apostrophe 's

  • We add apostrophe 's to a name to show possession, that something belongs to someone.
  • Zain's bag, Kashaf's pen, cousin's bicycle, teacher's book, Areeba's dress, Asma's dress.

Key Points

  • 'Zain's bag' means the bag belongs to Zain.
  • The apostrophe comes right after the name, before the letter s.

lessons.title: 4.3.3 Use of Articles 'a' or 'an'
lessons.notes_html:
A and An

Key Points

  • Look at the first sound of the word to choose 'a' or 'an'.

lessons.title: 4.4.1 Rhyming Words
lessons.notes_html:
Rhyming Words in the Poem

  • Rhyming words have the same ending sound.
  • dear : year. 'Seasons, seasons, in the year.'
  • light : bright. 'Summer comes with sunshine bright.'
  • crown : down and brown. 'In Autumn yellow leaves fall down, dry and crunchy, broken and brown.'
  • share : air. 'Winter, with cold mornings and icy air.'
  • broom : gloom. 'All are happy no one glooms.'

Key Points

  • Rhyming words make a poem musical and easy to remember.

lessons.title: 4.4.2 Picture Story
lessons.notes_html:
The Little Mouse and the Big Lion

  • Once a little mouse ran over a big sleeping lion. The lion woke up and caught the mouse.
  • The mouse said: Please let me go. One day I will help you. The lion laughed and let it go.

  • The mouse came and cut the ropes with its teeth. The lion became free and thanked the mouse.

Practice Note

This is a picture-story telling practice lesson. Look at the six pictures in your book and tell the story in simple sentences.

Key Points

  • Even small and weak friends can help us in need.
  • We should be kind to everyone; a good deed is never wasted.

lessons.title: 5.1 Seeking Permission (May I...?)
lessons.notes_html:
Asking Permission

  • We ask permission politely with 'May I...?' and 'please'.
  • Alice asks her mother at the market: Mother, may I have some samosas, please?
  • Mother says: No, Alice. This is an unhealthy food. You will get sick after eating it.
  • Ajay asks: Rahim, may I eat some fruits? Rahim says: Yes, Ajay. Fruits are very healthy to eat. They keep us strong and active.

Practice Note

This is a speaking-practice dialogue. Practise asking permission politely with 'May I... please?' in pairs.

Key Points

  • Always ask permission politely before taking or eating something.
  • Healthy food keeps us strong and active; unhealthy food can make us sick.

lessons.title: 5.2 Alice Feels Sick
lessons.notes_html:
Why Alice Fell Sick

  • Alice ate chips, burgers and samosas at school. These are unhealthy foods.
  • Her stomach hurt a lot, so her mother took her to Dr. Vijay.
  • Alice felt sorry because yummy food is not always good for health.

Healthy and Unhealthy Food

  • Healthy: fruits, vegetables, milk, bread, butter, broccoli, carrot, apple, meat, fish, watermelon, banana, yogurt, boiled eggs and chicken.
  • Unhealthy: cola, burger, lollipop, ice-cream, fries, candies, chocolate, pizza, chips and cold drinks.

Healthy Habits

  • Eating fruits and vegetables, taking a bath every day, washing hands before eating and sleeping on time keep us healthy.
  • Skipping breakfast, not cutting nails regularly, reading in dim light, watching too much TV and not brushing teeth are unhealthy habits.

The Promise

  • Alice promised Dr. Vijay: 'I will eat healthy food from now.'

Key Points

  • Healthy food makes us strong and active.
  • Too much junk food makes us sick.

lessons.title: 5.3.1 Showing Possession (Our, Your, Their)
lessons.notes_html:
Possessive Words

  • Possessive words show that something belongs to someone.
  • We : our. 'We say goodbye to our parents before going to school.'
  • They : their. 'They are sisters. That is their school.'
  • You : your. 'You are in my class. I am your teacher.'

More Possessives

  • I : my, He : his, She : her, You : your, It : its.

Key Points

  • Use 'our' for ourselves, 'your' for the person we talk to, and 'their' for other people.

lessons.title: 5.4.1 Re-write Sentences

lessons.title: 6.2.2 Good Touch and Bad Touch
lessons.notes_html:
Good Touch

  • A good touch is a respectful and caring touch that makes us feel secure and comfortable.
  • Examples: a hug from parents, a hi-five from friends, and holding hands with parents, siblings or friends while crossing the road.
  • Mother touching your cheeks, your sister tickling you in play, a friend putting a hand on your shoulder, your father kissing your forehead and your brother giving you a gift are good touches.

Bad Touch

  • A bad touch is any touch that feels unwanted, uncomfortable or forceful.
  • Examples: someone unknown hugs you, being hit or punched by someone unknown, and shaking hands with someone unknown.
  • Any touch we do not like is a bad touch, even from someone we know.

What To Do

  • Say 'No' loudly, move away, push the hands off our body, scream 'help' loudly, and run to a trusted adult and tell him or her at once.

Key Points

  • A good touch makes us feel happy and safe; a bad touch makes us feel sad and unsafe.

lessons.title: 6.3.2 Command and Request
lessons.notes_html:
Command and Request

  • A command is used to order someone to do something: 'Open the door.'
  • A request is used to ask someone politely. We add 'please' to make a request: 'Please open the door.' 'Please do not open the door.'

Examples

  • Command: Bring a glass of water. Request: Bring a glass of water, please.
  • Command: Give me the book. Request: Give me the book, please.
  • Command: Go to your class. Request: Please go to your class.

Key Points

  • Every sentence with 'please' is a request.
  • We write 'C' for command and 'R' for request.

mcqs.q: A command is used to:
mcqs.why: Commands are used to order someone to do something, while requests ask politely.

mcqs.q: A command becomes a request when we add the word:
mcqs.why: We add 'please' to make a request: 'Please open the door.'

mcqs.q: 'Open the door' as a request becomes:
mcqs.why: Adding 'please' changes the command 'Open the door' into the request 'Please open the door.'

mcqs.why: 'Open the book' has no 'please', so it is a command; we write C for it.

mcqs.why: It has the word 'please', so 'Please help me' is a request; we write R for it.

mcqs.why: 'Throw the garbage' orders someone and has no 'please', so it is a command.

lessons.title: 6.4.1 Command and Request Sentences
lessons.notes_html:
Making Commands and Requests

  • With go (the book's example): Command : Go to your room. Request : Go to your room, please.
  • With close: Close the door. / Do not close the door. Requests: Close the door, please. / Please do not close the door.
  • With watch: Watch the board. / Do not watch TV. Requests: Watch the board, please. / Please do not watch TV.
  • With play: Play in the park. / Do not play on the road. Requests: Play in the park, please. / Please do not play on the road.
  • With catch: Catch the ball. / Do not catch the frog. Requests: Catch the ball, please. / Please do not catch the frog.

Key Points

  • A negative command begins with 'Do not'.
  • Add 'please' to a command to change it into a request.

mcqs.why: A negative command begins with 'Do not': 'Do not close the door.'

lessons.title: 7.2 Unity in Diversity (Story)
lessons.notes_html:
The Race

  • Students from all over Pakistan joined an annual race competition.
  • Saima ran very fast and was ahead of all, but she fell down, got hurt and cried.
  • Marvi helped first. Then Zainab, Gulnaz and Nazia also helped Saima stand up.

The Winners

  • The judges saw the girls helping each other, clapped for them and announced: 'You all are winners.'
  • All the girls got trophies.
  • At the end all the girls said: 'We are from different provinces, yet we make one nation.'

Story Order

  • First: Saima ran very fast. Second: Saima stumbled and fell down. Third: Marvi helped Saima. Fourth: Zainab and Gulnaz helped Saima. Fifth: Nazia came to help Saima. Sixth: The judges saw the girls helping each other. Seventh: The judges gave them the trophies. Last: All the girls said, 'yet we make one nation.'

More About Pakistan

  • Karachi is the famous city of Sindh. Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan.
  • Pakistan's flag has two colours, green and white, with a white crescent and a star in the green part.

Key Points

  • Helping others is more important than winning a race.
  • We are from different provinces, yet we make one nation.

mcqs.why: Marvi helped first, Zainab and Gulnaz also gave their hands, and then Nazia also joined them to help Saima.

mcqs.why: The judges announced, 'You all are winners,' so all the girls won the race in the end.

mcqs.why: The judges saw their spirit of helping, clapped for them and gave trophies to all the girls.

mcqs.q: What did all the girls say in the end?

mcqs.why: All the girls said, 'We are from different provinces, yet we make one nation,' which shows unity in diversity.

mcqs.why: Islamabad is the capital city of Pakistan; Karachi is the famous city of Sindh.

lessons.title: 7.3.1 Opposite Describing Words
lessons.notes_html:
Opposite Pairs

  • young : old, tall : small (as matched in the book), left : right, up : down
  • easy : hard, friend : enemy, bright : dim

Sentences with Opposites

  • My grandfather is old, but my little brother is young.
  • The bird flies up and the leaves fall down.

  • Ali is my friend, not my enemy.
  • The sun is bright, but the old lamp is dim.
  • The school is on my left and the park is on my right.

  • Opposite words can be used together in one sentence to compare two things.
  • The book's example is: 'Aslam is a tall boy but Ali is a small student in the class.'

lessons.title: 7.3.2 Use of Prepositions
lessons.notes_html:
Prepositions of Place

  • Prepositions show the place or position of a thing.
  • The book is on the table. The fish is in the water.
  • The dog jumps over the wall. The cat is under the table.
  • The cat is near the box, sitting beside the box.

The Cat and the Box

  • in the box (inside), near the box (beside), over the box (jumping above), on the box (on top), under the box (below).

Key Points

  • in, on, under, over and near are prepositions of place.

mcqs.why: Prepositions show the place or position of a thing, like on, in, under and over.

mcqs.why: Inside means 'in', so the sentence is 'The cat is in the box.'

mcqs.q: The cat is sitting beside the box. Complete: 'The cat is ____ the box.'
mcqs.why: Beside the box means near the box, so we say 'The cat is near the box.'

mcqs.why: Jumping above the box is 'over', so the sentence is 'The cat jumps over the box.'

mcqs.q: The cat is sitting on top of the box. Complete: 'The cat is ____ the box.'
mcqs.why: On top of the box means 'on', so the sentence is 'The cat is on the box.'

mcqs.why: Under is a preposition of place; cat, box and table are naming words.

lessons.title: 7.4.1 Describing a Series of Three Pictures
lessons.notes_html:
The Bundle of Sticks

  • Three brothers always quarrelled with each other. Their old father was very sad.
  • The father gave one stick to each son, and they broke the sticks easily.
  • Then he gave them a bundle of sticks, but no one could break the bundle.
  • The father said: 'If you stay together like this bundle, no one can break you.'
  • From that day the brothers stopped fighting and lived together happily.

Practice Note

This is a picture-story telling practice lesson. Look at the three pictures in your book and tell the story in simple sentences.

Key Points

  • There is strength in unity.
  • Alone we are weak like a single stick; together we are strong like the bundle.

lessons.title: 7.4.2 Completing the Story

Complete the Story

  • 'Try to break it,' he ordered. Each son broke his stick easily. Later, he gave them a bundle of sticks. Each son used all their strength. But the bundle was too strong to break.
  • 'When you stay together like the bundle, no one can break you. But if you fight and stay apart, you will be weak.' The sons understood. From that day, they stopped fighting and lived together.

mcqs.why: Pronouns are words used in place of nouns, like I, we, you, he, she, it and they.

mcqs.q: 'Ordinal' numbers show:
mcqs.why: Ordinal means showing position, like first, second and third in a line.

mcqs.q: 'Recite' means:
mcqs.why: Recite means to say a poem or lesson aloud from memory, as we recite the rhymes.

mcqs.q: 'Rhyme' words have the same:
mcqs.why: Rhyme words have the same ending sound, like year and dear in the seasons poem.

mcqs.q: 'Flu' is:
options: an illness like a bad cold with fever
mcqs.why: Flu is an illness like a bad cold with fever; Zain gets flu in winter.

mcqs.q: 'Stomach' is the part of the body where ____ goes.
mcqs.why: The stomach is the part of the body where food goes; Alice's stomach hurt in the story.

mcqs.q: 'Vocabulary' means:
options: all the words we know and use
mcqs.why: Vocabulary means all the words we know and use; every lesson adds new words to it.
